key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating gave the best high-temperature oxidation resistance on SA516 boiler steel by forming a dense, protective oxide scale.
engineering_relevance: For boiler and hot-section components, HVOF Ni-Cr-based composite coatings can greatly reduce oxidation-driven degradation and extend service life.
method: Coated SA516 steel with Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN using HVOF and plasma spray.
Ran cyclic air oxidation for 50 cycles at 900°C.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating reduced maximum weight gain by 95.71% relative to uncoated SA516 steel and showed protective oxides such as Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated under laboratory cyclic oxidation only, so real-service durability under thermal shock, erosion, or longer exposures still needs validation.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
